function.mechanism: Phosphate modification changes starch functionality for texture/process stability; in vivo, modified starches are largely hydrolyzed and then fermented to short-chain fatty acids.

adi.basis: EFSA (2017) concluded there is no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for the general population and no need for a numerical ADI.

efsa.key_finding: Re-evaluation of modified starches (including E1410) found no general-population safety concern at reported uses/use levels; however, EFSA noted insufficient data for some infant special medical-formula uses.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA monostarch phosphate record lists ADI NOT SPECIFIED (including 2016); 2018 entry was specification-only.

concerns.summary: In modified-starch group studies reviewed by EFSA, renal mineralization findings appeared at high dietary levels, but were also seen with unmodified starch and were not considered relevant for human risk assessment.

EFSA reported that available data were insufficient to adequately assess certain uses (including E1410-containing categories) in infants/young children consuming foods for special medical purposes and special formulae at current maximum levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA found no safety concern for the general population at reported uses/use levels for modified starches including E1410.
EFSA concluded modified starches do not raise genotoxic concern based on in silico analysis.
JECFA assigned ADI not specified for monostarch phosphate.

adi_exceedance.notes: A numerical ADI was not set (EFSA/JECFA non-numeric outcome), so standard ADI exceedance calculations are not directly applicable; subgroup uncertainty exists for some infant medical-formula uses.

risk_assessment.rationale: General-population risk appears low under authorized uses, but EFSA identified a specific vulnerability/data-gap area (certain infant medical-formula uses), and E1410-specific toxicology is partly inferred from modified-starch group read-across.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no general-population safety concern and no numerical ADI needed
EFSA caveat for infants/young children in specific FSMP/formula categories
